```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
options(width = 70, useFancyQuotes = FALSE, pillar.width = 70)

finance_raw <- read.csv("data/finance_example.csv", check.names = FALSE)
names(finance_raw)[1] <- "ticker"

fin_plot <- as_tibble(finance_raw) |>
  select(ticker, sector = Sector, revenue = Revenue,
         net_margin = `Net Profit Margin`, market_cap = `Market Cap`,
         price_change_2015 = `2015 PRICE VAR [%]`) |>
  filter(revenue > 0, !is.na(net_margin)) |>
  mutate(super_sector = case_when(
    sector %in% c("Basic Materials", "Consumer Cyclical",
                  "Financial Services", "Real Estate")           ~ "Cyclical",
    sector %in% c("Consumer Defensive", "Healthcare", "Utilities") ~ "Defensive",
    sector %in% c("Communication Services", "Energy",
                  "Industrials", "Technology")                     ~ "Sensitive"))
```

## Session Objectives

By the end of this session, you will be able to:

1. Make quick plots with base R: `hist()`, `plot()`, `boxplot()`, `barplot()`
2. Explain the grammar of graphics: data, aesthetics, and geoms, built in layers
3. Make histograms, scatter plots, and side-by-side boxplots with `ggplot2`
4. Zoom in on a plot without silently dropping data
5. Use color and `facet_wrap()` to compare groups
6. Polish a figure for publication and save it with `ggsave()`

## The Data and Why We Plot

`fin_plot`: the finance data from Sessions 5--6, firms with positive revenue and a net margin, plus `super_sector`

### Plot before you model {.example}
A table of medians would never show a $96 trillion company, or net margins of minus 300,000%. A plot shows every observation at once.

# Quick Looks with Base R {#sec-base}

## `hist()`: One Numeric Variable

```{r}
#| label: base-hist

hist(fin_plot$net_margin)
```

- One bar: a few extreme values stretch the axis so far that almost every firm lands in it

## Look at the Middle, and Say So

```{r}
#| label: base-hist-middle

middle <- fin_plot$net_margin[fin_plot$net_margin > -1 & fin_plot$net_margin < 1]
hist(middle, breaks = 50, col = "steelblue",
     main = "Net margin, firms between -100% and +100%", xlab = "Net margin")
```

## `plot()`: Two Numeric Variables

```{r}
#| label: base-plot

ok <- fin_plot$market_cap > 0 & !is.na(fin_plot$market_cap)       # log needs > 0
plot(fin_plot$revenue[ok], fin_plot$market_cap[ok], log = "xy",
     xlab = "Revenue (USD)", ylab = "Market cap (USD)",
     pch = 16, col = rgb(0, 0, 1, alpha = 0.2))                   # transparent dots
```

- **Log scale**: each step is ten times the previous one; spreads out skewed data

## `boxplot()`: Side by Side, with Variable Width

```{r}
#| label: base-boxplot
#| fig-height: 3

par(mar = c(4, 11, 1, 1))                         # wide left margin for names
boxplot(net_margin ~ sector, data = fin_plot, horizontal = TRUE, las = 1,
        varwidth = TRUE, ylim = c(-1, 1), xlab = "Net margin", ylab = "")
```

- `varwidth = TRUE`: box width shows group size. `ylim` **zooms**: boxes use all data

## `barplot()` and Common Arguments

```{r}
#| label: base-barplot
#| fig-height: 2.6

par(mar = c(4, 11, 1, 1))
barplot(sort(table(fin_plot$sector)), horiz = TRUE, las = 1, xlab = "Number of firms")
```

- `main`, `xlab`, `ylab`, `col`, `xlim`, `ylim`, `log = "xy"`, `las = 1`, `par(mar = )`

# The Grammar of Graphics {#sec-grammar}

## Data + Aesthetics + Geoms, in Layers

| Piece | What it is | Example |
|------------------------|------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Data** | A (tidy) data frame | `fin_plot` |
| **Aesthetics** `aes()` | Column to visual property | `aes(x = revenue, y = market_cap)` |
| **Geoms** `geom_*()` | The type of mark | `geom_point()` |

```{r}
#| label: grammar
#| fig-height: 1.9

ggplot(fin_plot, aes(x = net_margin)) +      # data and aesthetics: an empty canvas
  geom_histogram(bins = 50)                   # a layer of bars
```

## `+`, not `|>`

### ggplot2 is older than the pipe {.alert}
Layers are joined with `+`, at the **end** of each line. A pipe can lead **into** a plot; after `ggplot()`, every step is `+`.

```{r}
#| label: pipe-into
#| fig-height: 1.9

fin_plot |>
  filter(net_margin > -1, net_margin < 1) |>    # filter explicitly, and say so
  ggplot(aes(x = net_margin)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50)
```

## What ggplot2 Offers

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
| Chart | Geom |
|----------------------|------------------------|
| Histogram | `geom_histogram()` |
| Density curve | `geom_density()` |
| Scatter plot | `geom_point()` |
| Trend line | `geom_smooth()` |
| Boxplot | `geom_boxplot()` |
| Violin plot | `geom_violin()` |
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
| Chart | Geom |
|----------------------|------------------------|
| Bars of counts | `geom_bar()` |
| Bars of values | `geom_col()` |
| Line (over time) | `geom_line()` |
| Heatmap | `geom_tile()` |
| Text labels | `geom_text()` |
:::
::::

- All work the same way. See the ggplot2 reference and the Posit cheatsheet

# Zooming without Dropping Data {#sec-zoom}

## `coord_cartesian()` Zooms

```{r}
#| label: zoom-coord
#| fig-height: 2.7

ggplot(fin_plot, aes(x = net_margin, y = sector)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1, 1))           # like a camera: all firms still used
```

## Scale Limits Drop Data

```{r}
#| label: zoom-limits
#| fig-height: 2.7

ggplot(fin_plot, aes(x = net_margin, y = sector)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1))      # removes firms BEFORE computing boxes
```

## Healthcare's Median Moved from a Loss to a Profit

```{r}
#| label: zoom-medians

fin_plot |>
  filter(sector == "Healthcare") |>
  summarise(median_all_firms     = median(net_margin),
            median_within_limits = median(net_margin[net_margin >= -1 & net_margin <= 1]))
```

### Zoom with `coord_cartesian()` {.alert}
Scale limits (`xlim()`, `ylim()`, `scale_*(limits = )`) silently drop data and change boxes, medians, and trend lines. To exclude observations, filter explicitly and report it.

# Scatter Plots {#sec-scatter}

## Points and Log Scales

```{r}
#| label: scatter

fin_scatter <- fin_plot |> filter(market_cap > 0)

ggplot(fin_scatter, aes(x = revenue, y = market_cap)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +                  # transparency shows overlap
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10()
```

## Adding a Trend Line

```{r}
#| label: scatter-smooth

ggplot(fin_scatter, aes(x = revenue, y = market_cap)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +   # straight line; band = confidence interval
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10()
```

## Mapping vs. Setting Color

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Mapped** inside `aes()`: shows data, adds a legend

```{r}
#| label: color-map
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 3
#| out-width: "100%"

ggplot(fin_scatter, aes(revenue, market_cap,
                        color = super_sector)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10()
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Set** outside `aes()`: one color for all

```{r}
#| label: color-set
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 3
#| out-width: "100%"

ggplot(fin_scatter, aes(revenue, market_cap)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4,
             color = "steelblue") +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10()
```
:::
::::

# Side-by-Side Boxplots {#sec-boxplot}

## Ordered, Horizontal, Variable Width

```{r}
#| label: boxplot-final
#| fig-height: 2.8

ggplot(fin_plot, aes(x = net_margin, y = fct_reorder(sector, net_margin))) +  # order by median
  geom_boxplot(varwidth = TRUE) +                                              # width = group size
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1, 1))                                             # zoom, do not drop
```

## Reading the Boxplots

- **Order** (`fct_reorder()`): Healthcare has the lowest median margin, Financial Services the highest
- **Width** (`varwidth = TRUE`): Financial Services is the largest sector, Communication Services the smallest
- **Horizontal**: long sector names stay readable

### The same plot in base R {.example}
`boxplot(net_margin ~ sector, data = fin_plot, horizontal = TRUE, varwidth = TRUE, ylim = c(-1, 1))`

# Small Multiples with `facet_wrap()` {#sec-facets}

## One Panel per Group

```{r}
#| label: facets

ggplot(fin_scatter, aes(x = revenue, y = market_cap)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ super_sector)                  # same axes, easy to compare
```

# Publication-Ready Figures {#sec-publication}

## Labels, Scales, Theme, and Colors

```{r}
#| label: publication-plot

dollar_short <- scales::label_dollar(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())  # $1B, not 1e+09

p_final <- ggplot(fin_scatter, aes(revenue, market_cap, color = super_sector)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = dollar_short) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = dollar_short) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(end = 0.85) +                  # colorblind-friendly
  labs(title   = "Larger firms are worth more, across all super sectors",
       x = "Revenue (log scale)", y = "Market capitalization (log scale)",
       color = "Super sector",
       caption = "Source: financial statements of US-listed firms, 2014.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## The Result

```{r}
#| label: publication-show
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 3.2
#| out-width: "65%"

p_final
```

- A title that **states the finding** tells the reader what to see

## Saving with `ggsave()`

```{r}
#| label: ggsave

dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave("output/revenue_marketcap.png", p_final, width = 6.5, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
ggsave("output/revenue_marketcap.pdf", p_final, width = 6.5, height = 4.5)
```

| Format | Type | Use it for |
|----------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| PDF | Vector: sharp at any zoom | LaTeX papers; journals accepting vector figures |
| PNG | Raster: pixels | Word, PowerPoint, web; `dpi = 300`+ for print |
| TIFF | Raster | Some journals: `dpi = 600, compression = "lzw"` |

- Size in inches = size in the document (single column about 3.5 in, full width about 7 in)

# Your Turn {#sec-your-turn}

## Exercise

### Tasks (use `fin_plot`) {.alert}
1. **Base R histogram** of `price_change_2015` for firms between -100% and +200%; 40 bars, title, label
2. **Base R boxplots** of `price_change_2015` by `super_sector`, `varwidth`, zoomed to -100 to 100. Lowest median?
3. **ggplot2 boxplots** by `sector`: horizontal, ordered, `varwidth`, `coord_cartesian()`. Which sector stands out?
4. **Scatter:** `price_change_2015` vs. `net_margin` with a trend line. First all firms, zoomed: where is the line? Then **filter** to typical firms (margins -1 to 1, price changes -100 to 200) and facet by `super_sector`
5. **Publish it:** a title stating the finding, `scales::label_percent()`, a caption, `theme_minimal()`; save as `output/margin_price.png`

## Exercise: Solution (1--2)

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| label: exercise-solution-1
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 3
#| out-width: "100%"

pc <- fin_plot$price_change_2015
hist(pc[pc > -100 & pc < 200], breaks = 40,
     main = "2015 price change",
     xlab = "Price change (%)", col = "grey70")
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| label: exercise-solution-2
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 3
#| out-width: "100%"

boxplot(price_change_2015 ~ super_sector,
        data = fin_plot, varwidth = TRUE,
        ylim = c(-100, 100), xlab = "",
        ylab = "Price change (%)")
```
:::
::::

- Lowest median: **Sensitive**, which includes Energy

## Exercise: Solution (3)

```{r}
#| label: exercise-solution-3
#| fig-height: 2.8

ggplot(fin_plot, aes(x = price_change_2015, y = fct_reorder(sector, price_change_2015))) +
  geom_boxplot(varwidth = TRUE) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-100, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Price change in 2015 (%)", y = NULL)
```

- **Energy**, far below every other sector: the 2014--2015 oil price collapse

## Exercise: Solution (4), All Firms

```{r}
#| label: exercise-solution-4a

ggplot(fin_plot, aes(x = net_margin, y = price_change_2015)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-100, 200))
```

- The line is fitted to **all** firms: a price change of over 2 million percent pulls it off the plot

## Exercise: Solution (4), Typical Firms

```{r}
#| label: exercise-solution-4b

fin_typical <- fin_plot |>
  filter(between(net_margin, -1, 1), between(price_change_2015, -100, 200))

p_margin <- ggplot(fin_typical, aes(x = net_margin, y = price_change_2015)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x)

p_margin + facet_wrap(~ super_sector)
```

- Upward for Cyclical and Defensive; nearly flat for Sensitive. Report how many firms you excluded

## Exercise: Solution (5)

```{r}
#| label: exercise-solution-5

p_margin_final <- p_margin +
  facet_wrap(~ super_sector) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +   # labels only: drops nothing
  labs(title   = "More profitable firms saw larger price gains in 2015, except in Sensitive sectors",
       x = "Net margin, 2014", y = "Stock price change in 2015 (%)",
       caption = "Excludes firms with net margins outside -100% to 100%\nor price changes outside -100% to 200%.") +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("output/margin_price.png", p_margin_final, width = 6.5, height = 4, dpi = 300)
```

# Summary {#sec-summary}

## Key Takeaways

- **Plot before you model**: plots show what summaries hide
- **Base R** for quick looks; `boxplot(varwidth = TRUE)` shows group sizes
- **ggplot2**: data + `aes()` + geoms, in layers joined with `+`
- **Zoom with `coord_cartesian()`**; scale limits silently drop data
- **Scatter**: log scales, `alpha`, `geom_smooth()`; color inside `aes()` maps, outside sets
- **Boxplots**: `fct_reorder()`, names on the y-axis, `varwidth = TRUE`
- **`facet_wrap()`**: one panel per group
- **Publish**: a title that states the finding, `scales` labels, a clean theme, viridis, `ggsave()`
